Do you want to continue? [Y/n] So there is some of my wasted space. But why are these automatically installed dependencies still installed? A: sendmail is a meta package consisting of a set of dependencies. When you install the sendmail metapackage it installs sendmail-bin, amongst other things. This provides a recommended package for cron, for example, but I believe there are also some other packages that recommend packages in the sendmail dependency chain. Autoremove will not remove auto packages which are recommended by other packages. You can change this behaviour by, for example, adding this apt configuration in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99_norec APT::AutoRemove::RecommendsImportant "false"; APT::AutoRemove::SuggestsImportant "false"; Then run apt-get remove --auto-remove sendmail, and you should see all your sendmail dependant packages being marked for removal, along with some other unrelated things which are now removal candidates due to the overall change in the apt configuration.
